title: Dex Agents CLI configuration
description: The configuration file of a Dex Agents CLI command, ~/.dex/agents/<harness>.yaml by default. It is YAML 1.2; this schema checks the parsed value. Every harness command in Python and TypeScript reads the same common fields and its own harness section. Do not put secrets in this file: provider keys come from the environment, and connector credentials stay in the connections that Dex Web authorizes. The schema cannot enforce this inside the open harness sections. Omit a field to take its default; null is never a valid value. The settings of one session may change model and system_prompt and may only narrow the rest; see session-settings.schema.json.
$comment: Patterns end with (?![\s\S]) rather than $, because Python's re lets $ match before a trailing newline and ECMAScript does not. The not schema repeats properties so that Ajv's strictRequired mode accepts it.

model.description: The model the agent calls, in the harness's own format, such as claude-opus-5-5 or a <provider>/<model> ID. Omitted: the harness command's default model. A harness command without a default model refuses to run until this is set.

system_prompt.description: The agent's instructions. Omitted, together with system_prompt_file: the harness's default instructions. Mutually exclusive with system_prompt_file.

system_prompt_file.description: A UTF-8 text file whose content is the agent's instructions, read when the command starts. A leading ~ means the home directory; a relative path is relative to the directory of this configuration file. Mutually exclusive with system_prompt.

dex.description: The Dex server the Worker connects to.

server.description: auto: reuse the running dexcli dev server of this machine, or start one. Otherwise the http or https URL of a Dex server, without user info. Its host is a DNS name whose last label starts with a letter, a dotted IPv4 address, or a bracketed IPv6 address. After the schema, the runtime also checks that each IPv4 part is 0 or a decimal from 1 to 255 without a leading zero, that an IPv6 address is valid, that no DNS label starts with xn--, and that the port is at most 65535.

connectors.description: The connector tools the agent may call.

mcp.description: The connectors MCP server. auto: the server that dexcli dev provides. Otherwise its http or https URL on a loopback host: 127.0.0.1, localhost, or [::1], without user info. After the schema, the runtime also checks that the port is at most 65535.

enabled.description: The connections whose operations the agent may call. Omitted: every authorized connection, with every operation its connector offers to agents. An empty list: no connector tools. An entry names a connector, which covers all of its connections, or connector/connection. A single-key map {"connector/connection": {"tools": [...]}} or {"connector": {"tools": [...]}} also limits the operations. Two entries must not cover the same connection.

approval.description: Approval beyond what each tool already requires.

always.description: Tool names, as the agent sees them, whose every call waits for approval, in addition to the tools whose connector or local tool policy asks for it.

workspace.description: The only directory the local file tools may read and write, and the working directory of shell commands. A leading ~ means the home directory; a relative path is relative to the directory of this configuration file.

local_tools.description: Tools that act on this machine. Reads run without approval; writes, browser clicks, form fills, and submits wait for approval; each shell command waits for approval unless it matches the allow list.

files.description: Read, write, list, and search files inside workspace.

enabled.description: Whether the agent may run shell commands at all.

allow.description: Commands that run without approval. A command matches only when its whole text equals an entry exactly; every other command waits for approval.

browser.description: Drive a local browser. The browser is downloaded the first time the agent uses it.

media.description: Where the images of a session are stored: the images attached with /image and the images that connector tools return. Session state keeps only a reference to each image; the bytes stay in this store, one copy per distinct image, named by its SHA-256. Every Worker of a session must reach the same store. Sessions cannot change it: session settings ignore a media key with a warning. Credentials never go in this file: an s3 store reads them from the environment or the standard AWS chain.

store.description: auto: a directory on this machine, ~/.dex/agents/media, which keeps its own copy of each image, never a link to the original file. Otherwise s3://<bucket> or s3://<bucket>/<prefix> for an S3 bucket, which Workers on other machines can reach too. The bucket name has 3 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, dots, or hyphens and starts and ends with a letter or digit; the prefix is printable ASCII without spaces. An s3 store needs the S3 support of the agents library: the dex-agents[s3] extra in Python, the @aws-sdk/client-s3 package in TypeScript.

endpoint.description: The http or https URL of an S3-compatible service, such as http://127.0.0.1:9000; omitted, AWS S3. Only valid with an s3 store. With an endpoint, the bucket is addressed in the URL path, as most S3-compatible services need. The host rules and the runtime checks are those of dex.server.

claude.description: Options of the Claude Agent SDK command. Omitted: its defaults.

openai.description: Options of the OpenAI Agents SDK command. Omitted: its defaults.

pydantic_ai.description: Options of the Pydantic AI command. Omitted: its defaults.

deepagents.description: Options of the Deep Agents command. Omitted: its defaults.

google_adk.description: Options of the Google ADK command. Omitted: its defaults.

vercel_ai.description: Options of the Vercel AI SDK command. Omitted: its defaults.

mastra.description: Options of the Mastra command. Omitted: its defaults.

pi.description: Options of the Pi command. Omitted: its defaults.

builtin.description: Options of the built-in agent loop command. Omitted: its defaults.

model.description: A model ID in the harness's own format, such as claude-opus-5-5 or openai/gpt-5-mini. Any non-empty string; the harness checks it.

tool_name.description: A tool name: 1 to 128 ASCII letters, digits, underscores, hyphens, or dots.

operation_name.description: A connector operation: its snake-case name, such as get_message, or its operationId, such as getMessage. Both spellings name the same operation: an operationId is compared after the connectors library's lowerCamelToSnake conversion, which keeps acronym runs together, so listStoryIDs is list_story_ids and getHTTPResponse is get_http_response.

connector_key.description: A connector ID, or connector/connection. A connection name has at most 256 characters, no slash, no control character, and no leading or trailing space, as Dex Web requires.

tools.description: The connector operations the agent may call, by snake-case name or operationId. Two entries must not name the same operation.

harness_options.description: Harness options. Each harness command defines its own fields and ignores the sections of other harnesses.
